caption: A 7-segment display decoder: four input lines (a 4-bit number) light the seven segments of its hex digit, 0-9 then A b C d E F, in a 9x9 tower 18 high. Seven rings stacked every 2 levels, one per segment: four subtract comparators face the segment's lamp; each compares one row of the top two bits (its two sides read a3 and a2, or their inverses, from the ring's corners) with that row's function of the low two bits (its rear). Torch towers carry the inputs up the corners, fed by a wall-torch forest with repeater lines; each rear column is a torch chain (the inverse of the rear two levels down) plus injected a1/a0 terms. Catalog parts: comparator gates and torch inverters.

A 7-segment display decoder: four input lines (a 4-bit number) light the seven segments of its hex digit, 0-9 then A b C d E F, in a 7x7 tower 16 high. A chain of subtract comparators on top turns the four bits into one signal strength s = 15 - (8 a0' + 2 a1 + 4 a2 + a3); s flows down the tower losslessly through comparator bridges. Seven rings stacked every 2 levels, one per segment: each lamp is lit by window comparators (a hopper behind each sets its window, its sides read s and a copy of its complement), so each segment lights exactly for its set of strengths. Catalog parts: comparator gates (subtract) and constant hoppers.
